lenses.contested:
FOUR GENUINE DISAGREEMENTS. Do not paper over any of them.

1. ═══ THE BIG ONE: does super-Earth lithosphere get THINNER or THICKER? ═══
This determines the SIGN of Family C, the family the game most wants to know about.
• Incompressible (Boussinesq) side: higher Rayleigh number ⇒ thinner boundary layer. Valencia et al.
  (2006) state it directly from their interior models, and the marginal-stability result δ ∝ g^(−1/3)
  is unambiguous under Boussinesq assumptions. Valencia & O'Connell (2009) extend this to argue plate
  tectonics becomes MORE likely with planet size.
• Compressible side: Miyagoshi, Tachinami, Kameyama & Ogawa find that adiabatic compression
  'substantially reduces the vigor of thermal convection', that 'the lithosphere becomes much thicker
  and hot ascending plumes become thinner than expected from Boussinesq models' at 10 M_⊕, and that
  hot plumes lose buoyancy mid-mantle and never reach the surface at all.
• O'Neill & Lenardic (2007) argued from the other direction that super-Earths favour a STAGNANT LID.
If the compressible side is right, Family C's exponent flips from −0.85 toward 0 or positive, and a
super-Earth would have BROADER, not finer, flexural features — the exact opposite visual.
HONEST STATE: p_C ∈ [−0.9, +0.3]. My −0.85 assumes Boussinesq. I could NOT load the Miyagoshi papers
(redirect/auth wall), so I cannot adjudicate. RECOMMENDATION: implement Family C with the exponent as
a named constant and a comment stating both sides, not as a bare number. Do not let a UAT screenshot
decide this.

2. ═══ Is the ~10 km scale break universal, or does it vary 5× between near-twins? ═══
Landais et al. (2018) find the break at 10–20 km on Earth, Mars, Mercury AND the Moon and call it 'a
general property of all planetary topographies'. Crooks et al. find it at 10 km on Earth but 50 km on
Venus — a 5× spread between two planets of nearly identical radius and gravity. Both cannot be simply
true. Possible reconciliations: different estimators (Haar fluctuations vs. width-scaling), Venus's
much hotter and thicker elastic lithosphere genuinely being the driver (which would SUPPORT the T_e
interpretation while breaking the 'universal 10 km' claim), or Venus's deep gorges biasing the fit
(Crooks et al. flag this themselves). Note also that Crooks et al. is a 1998-dated preprint with no
journal venue I could find, and their Earth data is the continental US only — weaker evidence than
Landais et al. If Venus is right, the break tracks T_e and Family C's mechanism is confirmed even as
its 'universal 10 km' anchor dissolves.

3. ═══ Are plate sizes one power law or several subpopulations? ═══
Bird (2003) read the data as several fractal subpopulations. Sornette & Pisarenko (2003) argue a
single continuous power law (exponent 0.25 ± 0.05) with the 4π-steradian sum as the only cutoff.
Wilkinson et al. (2018) reject subpopulations again but propose exponentially distributed DIAMETERS
rather than a power law in area. All three make plate size a function of total sphere area — so
Family B's p ≈ 1.0 survives all three readings, which is why I use it. But the underlying
distribution SHAPE is unsettled, so do not build a plate-count or plate-size-histogram generator on
any one of them. And note the sample size: n = 1 planet, ever.

4. ═══ Nobody has ever seen a super-Earth's surface ═══
This must be stated to the owner plainly, because 'scientifically predicted' can be heard as
'observed'. There is no resolved image, no altimetry, no shape model, and no topographic spectrum for
any planet above 1 R_⊕. Every exponent above R = 1 in this brief is extrapolation from Solar-System
calibration. The Solar System offers exactly ONE body above 0.9 g (Earth itself), so the entire
super-Earth branch is anchored on a single point plus theory. The honest framing for the code comment
is: 'derived from Solar-System-calibrated physics; no observational constraint exists above 1 R_⊕.'

5. ═══ A smaller one worth flagging: the two crater systems in the repo may be inconsistent ═══
`bombardment.js` uses K_DT = 3.1 km with a HARD threshold on real km diameter. The lab's
`deriveUniforms` uses a separate `craterComplexD = kMorph/g` in CRATER-RADIUS units (kRocky = 0.9,
kIcy = 0.45) with smoothstep(0.6·D, D). These are different quantities in different units and I did
not verify they agree. Given that Pike's onset (K≈1.75) and flat-floor (K≈3.30) thresholds bracket a
factor of ~1.9, and the lab's smoothstep band is a factor of 1/0.6 = 1.67 wide, the SHAPES are
compatible — but somebody should check that the two paths produce the same morphology at the same g
before either is tuned further. Also note the icy switch (kIcy = 0.45, half of kRocky) implies icy
crusts transition at HALF the diameter of rock; Holsapple's Table 1 assigns Cold Ice μ = 0.55, the
same as hard rock, for the SIZE law — so the icy weakening is being asserted for the morphology law
without, as far as I could verify, a cited source. Worth checking separately.

  Earth-size planets likely do not support mountains surpassing 10 km."

WHY THE BREAK AT g = 1 IS PHYSICAL, NOT COSMETIC. relief = min(process supply, strength ceiling). Below 1 g
the ceiling is slack and supply binds: Melosh's own worked example over-predicts the Moon by >2x and he says
so ("Evidently strength is not the major factor limiting the Moon's topography: History must play a role").
Confirmed empirically: over Earth/Venus/Mars/Mercury/Moon, absolute relief is statistically UNCORRELATED with
g (log-log slope -0.068, r^2 = 0.015; without Venus, +0.004, r^2 = 0.000), with a 3.05x relief spread at
identical gravity (Mercury 9.85 vs Mars 30.0 km, both 0.377-0.378 g). A single global exponent is provably
wrong in both directions: Q = 1.588 fitted downward predicts 67 km of lunar relief (observed 19.9);
Q = 0.58 extrapolated upward predicts absolute relief RISING with size.

UNCERTAINTY. Q_hi in [1.33, 2.20] is defensible (Guimond+2022 cold-to-hot interior bracket). 1.588 is the
point where the strength route (1.588) and the convection route (1.68) agree to 5% having shared nothing but
the mass-radius relation -- a point of maximum agreement, not the centre of a measured distribution. Anything
below ~1.1 is not defensible. Y is uncertain by 5x (100 MPa granite -> ~500 MPa brittle-ductile max, Katayama
2021 via Guimond+2022) but that is a PREFACTOR and cancels exactly under Earth normalisation -- which is the
reason to keep normalising to Earth and never compute km from Y. Where the break sits is soft to ~1.5x in g;
smoothing the corner with a min() over the two branches is scientifically neutral, the exponents are not.

  CONSEQUENCE: a fixed-N spherical Voronoi whose cells scale with the body IS the physically correct construction.

  Adjudication, with evidence rather than averaging: Lichtenberg & Miguel 2024 (Treatise on Geochemistry 3rd ed.,
  arXiv:2405.04057) survey exactly this list and state the models are "not reaching convergence (Lenardic 2018)."
  There is no defensible formula. But the DISAGREEMENT ITSELF IS INFORMATIVE IN A SPECIFIC WAY: Valencia's water
  lever (halving yield strength by hydration == doubling planetary mass) and Korenaga's are the same lever, and
  all three camps accept it. So water/surface-T is the deterministic axis; radius is the contested one.
  LAW: P_mobile = f(volatileFraction, T_surf) * (1 + eps * ln R), eps drawn per-body from a seeded distribution
  on [-0.3, +0.3]. Radius enters only as a seeded, SIGN-AMBIGUOUS nudge. A hard deterministic P(R) would be
  asserting a resolution the field does not have. Solar-System prior (one-sided, and only constrains R < 1):
  every non-Earth terrestrial body is stagnant or episodic.

P4 — EACH REGIME MUST HAVE ITS OWN GENERATOR. This is the renderer's real contract, and fBm satisfies none of it.
  MOBILE: global CONNECTED network of narrow linear belts partitioning the sphere into ~7-15 plates; relief
    concentrated at boundaries (convergent ranges / divergent rifts / transform offsets); low-relief cratonic
    interiors; crater record erased.
  STAGNANT: NO global boundary network. Ancient crater size-frequency distribution + discrete volcanic constructs
    (shields, calderas, coronae, tessera) + long-wavelength degree-1/2 dynamic topography + isolated graben
    systems. Structurally SPARSE and patch/point-dominated. (Measured: Mercury, Mars, Moon, Venus.)
  EPISODIC: stagnant character overprinted by globally-synchronous resurfacing -> sharp-edged patchwork of
    very-young and very-old terrain. Venus's near-uniform crater age is the type case.
  Taxonomy: Lichtenberg & Miguel 2024 Fig. 11 (A1/A2/A3 plus plume-lid / squishy-lid / heat-pipe).
  >>> GENERIC fBm AS THE SOLE LOW/MID-FREQUENCY SOURCE IS WRONG IN BOTH REGIMES, AT EVERY RADIUS. Mobile: no
  boundary network, no plate interiors, no convergent/divergent asymmetry. Stagnant: crater-SFD + discrete
  constructs is not self-affine noise either. fBm's only defensible role is the sub-plate ROUGHNESS layer riding
  on a structured low-order field. There is no radius at which the current substitution becomes correct.

ONE CODEBASE FACT THAT BLOCKS ALL OF P3: e1Regime.js:56 gates the seeded mobile/episodic/stagnant draw to
massEarth in [0.6, 1.6], which under M ~ R^3.7 is R in [0.87, 1.14] R_E. EVERY super-Earth falls out of the
seeded band and is routed by lidStrength instead, whose only gravity term (gMod, clamped [0.90, 1.12]) saturates
at g ~ 1.9. Radius currently has almost no principled influence on regime -- and total influence on whether you
see plates at all, via the display crossover.
derivation.wavelengthLaw:
THERE IS NO SINGLE WAVELENGTH EXPONENT. Terrestrial topography carries SIX families with SIX different
R-dependences. Collapsing them into one number destroys the physics. Master form, per class k:

  lambda_k(R) = lambda_k,E * R^(p_k)   [km]      theta_k = lambda_k / (R * 6371) ~ R^(p_k - 1)   [rad on the disc]

The code hook featureFrequencyFromKm(R, L_km, c) = c*R*6371/L_km is ALREADY CORRECT, which means a fixed
featureSizeKm silently encodes p = 0. That is right for D/E/F and wrong for A/B.

A — GEOMETRIC / DEEP-MANTLE (hemispheric dichotomies, superplume provinces, continent-scale highlands,
    largest multi-ring basins).   p_A = +1.00 EXACTLY.  theta_A ~ R^0 (constant fraction of the disc).
    lambda_A = 2*pi*R_km / sqrt(l(l+1)), l = 1-2  =>  4.443*R_km (l=1), 2.565*R_km (l=2); 28,300 / 16,300 km at Earth.
    Jeans relation, Wieczorek 2007 (Treatise on Geophysics vol.10 ch.5). Degree l is DIMENSIONLESS and does not
    scale with R; physical wavelength at fixed l scales exactly as R. Never port a degree number as a km.
    Justification for l = 1-2: planetary topography spectra are red across Earth/Venus/Mars/Moon, so power always
    peaks at the lowest degrees, and the peak degree does not shift with planet size. This is the only exponent
    in the table with zero uncertainty -- it is sphere geometry.

B — CONVECTIVE CELL / PLATE / SLAB SPACING (tectonic provinces, orogen spacing, rift spacing, plate outlines).
    p_B = +1.10 +/- 0.15.  theta_B ~ R^+0.10, i.e. essentially constant on the disc.
    lambda_B = A_c * d_mantle, A_c in [2, 6]; d_mantle(Earth) = 2890 km; Earth's observed degree-2 is 5.65*d.
    d_mantle ~ R^1.05-1.20 from Valencia et al. 2006 Table 1 (D ~ M^0.286-0.316, R ~ M^0.263-0.272).
    Cells are far wider than Rayleigh-Benard onset (2.02*d rigid-rigid) because low-viscosity channels and
    continents push mantle flow to long wavelength -- hence the wide A_c bracket. Consistent with P1's L/R ~ const.

C — FLEXURAL / LITHOSPHERIC (mountain-range width, forebulge and trough spacing, wrinkle-ridge and graben
    spacing, the topographic roughness scale-break).   p_C = -0.85 SHIPPED, bracket [-0.9, 0.0]. CONTESTED.
    T_e = [Ra_c*kappa*eta / (rho*alpha*dT*g)]^(1/3) ~ g^(-1/3)  (marginal stability; standard, and independent of
    mantle depth -- which is precisely why it does NOT scale with R).
    lambda_flex = 2*pi*[E*T_e^3 / (3(1-nu^2)*drho*g)]^(1/4) ~ T_e^(3/4)*g^(-1/4) ~ g^(-1/2) ~ R^(-0.85).
    Earth anchor computed this run: T_e = 30 km, E = 100 GPa, nu = 0.25, drho = 2300, g = 9.81 => flexural
    parameter 81 km, lambda_flex = 507 km.
    OBSERVED cross-check, and it is a strong one: the topographic scale break sits at 10-20 km on Earth, Mars,
    Mercury AND the Moon -- bodies spanning 0.27-1.0 R_E (Landais, Schmidt & Lovejoy 2018, Icarus,
    doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2018.07.005, arXiv:1805.11249). Same absolute km on a 0.27 R_E body and a 1.0 R_E body
    falsifies "break ~ R" outright. Venus at 0.95 R_E has its crossover at 50 km, 5x Earth's (Crooks et al.,
    arXiv:1809.02457 -- PREPRINT, no journal venue found), which supports the T_e/thermal mechanism while
    dissolving the "universal 10 km" claim. Both readings point away from geometry and toward rheology.
    THE SIGN IS DISPUTED ABOVE ~5 M_E: Boussinesq/incompressible (Valencia et al. 2006, verbatim: "the thickness
    of the boundary layer decreases with increasing mass as a consequence of higher Rayleigh numbers") gives
    -0.85; compressible models (Miyagoshi/Tachinami/Kameyama/Ogawa series -- NOT RETRIEVED, redirect wall) report
    a much THICKER lithosphere at 10 M_E, which would push p_C toward 0 or positive. See maxDecisions #1.

D — IMPACT.
    D1 crater diameter at fixed impactor (gravity regime): D ~ g^(-mu/(2+mu)).
        mu = 0.4 dry sand/regolith -> -0.167;  mu = 0.55 wet and rocky targets, incl. Hard Rocks and Cold Ice
        -> -0.216. Holsapple 2022 (arXiv:2203.07476) §3.1-3.2 + Table 1. p_D1 = -0.28 (sand) to -0.37 (rock) in R.
        AUDIT: bombardment.js K_GS = 0.17 is the DRY-SAND value. A silicate or icy crust should use 0.216. The
        existing rockyCrust discriminator is the natural switch. Small, defensible, cited fix.
    D2 simple->complex transition: D_t = K_DT / g, K_DT = 3.1 km*g_E.  p_D2 = -1.70 in R.
        AUDIT: CONFIRMED CORRECT. Lunar transition ~19-20 km * g 0.165 = 3.1-3.3 (Silber, Osinski, Johnson &
        Grieve 2017, JGR-Planets, doi:10.1002/2016JE005236, arXiv:1704.04247). Pike's onset threshold is lower
        (D* = 10.6 km => K ~ 1.75) and rim-height higher (K ~ 3.76); 3.1 sits at the flat-floor/fully-complex end,
        the conservative choice. Verified this run: D_t = 1.56 km at R = 1.5, 0.95 km at R = 2.0.
        >>> THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST VISUALLY LEGIBLE SUPER-EARTH PREDICTION IN THE WHOLE SYNTHESIS: on a
        super-Earth essentially every resolvable crater is COMPLEX -- central peaks and terraces everywhere, no
        simple bowls. Known offset with a derivable sign: v_impact^2 = v_inf^2 + v_esc^2 and v_esc ~ R^1.35, so
        super-Earths impact harder; Mercury's observed onset already sits 1.5-2x above the pure-1/g prediction
        for this reason, so expect real super-Earth D_t 1.5-2x ABOVE 3.1/g.
    D3 crater size-frequency DISTRIBUTION SHAPE: p_D3 = 0.00 EXACTLY. The SFD is a property of the impactor
        population, not the target. Do not scale it with R. (Matches the existing dN/dg = 0 null law.)

E — AEOLIAN.  p_E = 0.00 in R AND in g. Gravity does not appear at all.
    lambda_dune = 53 * L_drag, L_drag = (rho_s/rho_f)*d_grain. Claudin & Andreotti 2006 (EPSL 252:30,
    arXiv:cond-mat/0603656) -- "a consistent scaling law lambda ~= 53*L_drag that covers almost five decades",
    tested in water, air, fresh snow, a high-pressure CO2 wind tunnel reproducing Venus, and martian dunes. Best-
    constrained item in the whole synthesis. Computed anchors: Earth 21 m; Mars 0.77 km.
    => duneSizeKm must be driven by ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY and grain size, never by R. A thick-atmosphere
    super-Earth gets FINER dunes than Earth; a thin-atmosphere one gets Mars-scale dunes.

F — FLUVIAL.  p_F = 0.00 in R and g.
    lambda_valley = (6.4 to 12.7)*L_c, L_c = (D/K)^(1/(2m+1)). Perron, Kirchner & Dietrich 2009 (Nature 460:502,
    doi:10.1038/nature08174). L_c is 10-100 m at the five measured sites. Set by climate and rock erodibility,
    and independent of erosion RATE -- so a more tectonically active planet gets MORE drainage, not coarser.

HEADLINE, and it is the opposite of the intuitive one: going up in R, only the two mantle-driven families keep
pace with the planet. Everything from the lithosphere outward -- flexure, craters, dunes, rivers -- is set by a
LOCAL physical scale that is constant or shrinking in km. A super-Earth reads as a FINER-GRAINED world at the
same disc size: the same number of continent-scale provinces, ~2x finer mountain texture, ~1.7x finer crater
texture, 1/R finer dunes and drainage, and a near-total absence of simple bowl craters.
DO NOT MODEL "bigger planet = bigger features."

CONFIDENCE ORDERING (most to least): A (exact geometry) > E (measured, 5 decades) > D2 (measured over 6x in g)
> D1/D3 (lab-measured pi-group scaling) > F (measured, Earth-only) > B (modelled, n=1 empirical check) > C
(modelled, sign disputed above ~5 M_E).
derivation.verdictRationale:
KEEP 0.58 for g <= 1. DO NOT extrapolate it above g = 1. Replace the upper branch with a derived exponent, and
drop RELIEF_FLOOR from 0.40 to 0.12 in the same edit or the fix silently reverts.

WHY KEEP IT BELOW 1 g. It is calibrated on the bodies the game actually draws in that range, it passes the
workstream's own band test, and it is continuous with Earth = 1 for free. Churning it buys nothing.

BUT RELABEL IT, BECAUSE IT IS NOT WHAT ITS COMMENT SAYS. The comment presents it as a strength-cap exponent.
It is not: over Earth/Venus/Mars/Mercury/Moon, absolute relief is statistically UNCORRELATED with gravity
(log-log slope -0.068, r^2 = 0.015; -0.004 and r^2 = 0.000 without Venus), while relief/R against R gives slope
-0.81, r^2 = 0.80. Mercury and Mars have effectively identical gravity (0.377 vs 0.378) and a 3.05x relief
difference. Q_RELIEF = 0.58 is a RADIUS PROXY IN GRAVITY'S CLOTHING. It has no predictive content in g. The
mislabelling is exactly what made the super-Earth extrapolation look sanctioned, so the comment change matters
more than the number.

WHY IT MUST NOT GO ABOVE 1 g -- three independent reasons, any one sufficient:
 1. SIGN ERROR. Under the lab's own g = R, E = g^-0.58 implies absolute relief h ~ R^0.42: super-Earths get MORE
    mountainous (19.8 km at 1.0 R_E -> 26.5 km at 2.0). Four independent physical arguments and every retrieved
    source say relief FALLS as ~1/g above Earth gravity. This is not a magnitude disagreement, it is a direction
    disagreement. Overshoot vs the derived law: 1.47x at 1.2 R_E, 2.04x at 1.4, 2.70x at 1.6, 4.34x at 2.0.
 2. WRONG PHYSICAL BRANCH. Relief = min(process supply, strength ceiling). Below 1 g the ceiling is slack and
    supply binds -- Melosh's own arithmetic over-predicts the Moon by more than 2x and he says so explicitly.
    At and above 1 g the ceiling comes down onto the supply and takes over. The g <= 1 anchors carry zero
    information about the branch that binds above 1 g.
 3. THE FIT WAS NEVER EVIDENCE FOR AN EXPONENT. calibration/relief-envelope.mjs fits five AUTHORED target values
    (no citation in the file for any of them) and reports band membership only -- no residual, no r^2, no
    standard error on Q. The bands are wide (Mars [0.003, 0.020], Moon [0.008, 0.050], Mimas [0.040, 0.150]), so
    "ALL PASS" would also be true for a wide range of Q. laws.js re-measures the same function, which is a drift
    guard, not an external check.

RELIEF_FLOOR = 0.40 MOVES FROM HARMLESS TO LOAD-BEARING AND MUST CHANGE IN THE SAME COMMIT. Its comment says it
"binds only g >~ 4.85" -- true at Q = 0.58, false at Q = 1.588, where it binds at g = 1.78, i.e. R = 1.40 R_E,
M = 3.5 M_E (verified this run). That is the middle of the population the directive is about; it would clamp the
entire super-Earth branch flat and silently reinstate the bug. Set FLOOR = 0.12 (binds only past R = 2.19 R_E,
M = 18 M_E) or remove it. It was never derived -- the calibration script's own comment says it was "kept at the
current gCap FLOOR (0.40)", inherited verbatim from the older guessed reliefGravityFactor clamp. RELIEF_CEIL =
133 is unaffected and still never binds.

TWO PREREQUISITES, WITHOUT WHICH THE FIX IS UNOBSERVABLE OR WRONG:
 (a) The shipped envelope is RADIUS-BLIND ON SCREEN. world-engine-lab.html:3016 stashes the CANONICAL preset
     gravity (deriveUniforms computes g = massEarth/radiusEarth^2 from the preset), and :5908 feeds that to
     uPerturb. Dragging the radius slider changes rendered relief amplitude by exactly zero -- while the comment
     at :5907 asserts "Radius flows through g via reliefEnvelope". Meanwhile deriveConditionVector on the CPU
     path DOES apply g = g_c*(R/R_c). Two different gravities for the same planet in the same frame.
 (b) Q_hi = 1.588 is correct ONLY if the g handed to reliefEnvelope is true self-compressed gravity. The lab
     supplies constant-density g (body-condition-vector.js:37, assumption stated in its own comment). Either fix
     g at source and use 1.588, or key the upper branch on R and use a*Q_hi = 2.700. Do not mix -- they encode
     identical physics but only one leaves the rest of the engine correct. Recommendation is the R form for the
     relief law (invariant to the g bug either way) PLUS the source fix, with a unit test asserting they agree.

Also unify the FIVE surviving copies of the older reliefGravityFactor(g) = clamp(g^-0.5, 0.40, 2.50)
(planet-lod-lab-core.js:1100, tectonic.js:167 private copy consumed at :137/:207, relief-e6-tectonic.js:67,
magmatism.js:118, plates.js:118/131). The CPU tectonic and magmatic relief currently use exponent 0.50 with
ceiling 2.5 and a floor binding at g = 6.25, while the shading envelope uses 0.58 with ceiling 133 and a floor
binding at g = 4.85. Neither has a stated source; 0.50 predates the calibration entirely. The repo answers the
same question two ways.
derivation.crossoverVerdict:
bakeReliefCrossover MUST BE DEMOTED FROM A CHARACTER DECISION TO A TEXEL-DENSITY LOD GUARD. Its current form is
the clearest instance in the codebase of a display lever deciding physics, and the code comment discloses the
defect in its own words: "RESIDUE (disclosed, D3): the baked continent PATTERN (incl. stamped basins) morphs
into the analytic body across the fade -- a visible change in continent CHARACTER, not size."

WHAT IT DOES NOW. uReliefBakeStrength = base * bakeReliefCrossover(sVis), with bakeReliefCrossover(s) =
1 - smoothstep(0, BAKE_CROSS_SPAN=1.0, |log2 s|) and sVis = visScaleOf(R) = R^0.5. So the baked cube -- which on
Rocky/Earthlike is exactly where the plate-Voronoi tectonics lives (writePlateUpliftSphere: continents, plate
boundaries, provinces) -- fades to zero at R >= 4 and is half-gone at R = 2, replaced by generic fbmd. Above
R ~ 4 a terrestrial planet's tectonic structure is replaced by noise BY CONSTRUCTION, for a rendering reason
(holding on-screen feature size constant), not a physical one. The project's own tracker already logs this from
Max's UAT with the same root cause (planet-lod-campaign-tracker.md:170-195).

WHY IT IS UNAMBIGUOUSLY WRONG UNDER THE LAWS ABOVE, not merely inelegant:
 - P1 says plate count is INVARIANT in R (N ~ R^-0.07) and plate angular size is invariant at ~16.6 deg. The
   structured plate pattern is the thing that should PERSIST at large R. The crossover deletes precisely the
   feature the physics says is scale-invariant.
 - P4 says fBm is the wrong low/mid-frequency field in BOTH regimes -- mobile (no boundary network) and stagnant
   (crater-SFD + discrete constructs, not self-affine). So there is no radius at which the substitution becomes
   defensible. It is not "less accurate at large R"; it is wrong everywhere it fires.
 - Family A/B say theta ~ R^0 to R^+0.10. The structure channel is ALREADY constant-on-screen if the wavelength
   law is implemented. The physics delivers, for free, the exact size-constancy property the crossover was
   hacking around. The crossover exists to solve a problem the correct law does not have.

WHAT REPLACES IT — four concrete moves:
 1. SPLIT THE BLEND INTO TWO CHANNELS. STRUCTURE (plate partition, regime signature, degree-1/2 dichotomy,
    stamped basins) and DETAIL (sub-plate roughness octaves). Structure weight = 1.0 at ALL radii, unconditionally.
    Crossover applies to DETAIL only.
 2. CLOSE THE ENGINEERING GAP THE COMMENT NAMES. The comment's stated justification is that the plate-Voronoi
    body "CANNOT be re-keyed by a display frequency ... NOT a noise frequency there is no domain hook for." That
    is a true statement about the current code and a false reason to discard the pattern. The fix is an analytic
    plate-Voronoi evaluator in the shader (or a higher-resolution / cascaded bake), so the structure channel
    survives magnification. That is the real work item this verdict creates.
 3. RE-KEY WHAT REMAINS ON A PHYSICAL TRIGGER. The detail crossover should be driven by TEXEL DENSITY -- baked
    cube face resolution vs screen-space sample rate -- not by |log2 sVis|. Then it is a genuine mip/LOD adequacy
    guard with a measurable trigger, and BAKE_CROSS_SPAN becomes an honest rendering tunable. sVis stops being an
    argument to it entirely.
 4. STOP LETTING DISPLAY SCALE SET THE WAVELENGTH DOMAIN. uDispDomainScale = sVis = R^0.5 is a display law
    masquerading as a physical one. Domain scale must come from the wavelength families: theta_k =
    lambda_k(R)/(R*6371), with p_A = +1.00, p_B = +1.10, p_C = -0.85, p_D1 = -0.37, p_D2 = -1.70, p_E = p_F = 0.
    Families C-F genuinely shrink on the disc as R grows. THAT SHRINKAGE IS THE PREDICTION, NOT AN ARTEFACT, AND
    MUST NOT BE CORRECTED AWAY. If a large planet reads as finer-grained, that is the science landing.

REDUCED TO ONE LINE: bakeReliefCrossover keeps its name and its smoothstep, loses sVis as its input, loses all
authority over the structure channel, and becomes a detail-octave LOD blend keyed on texel adequacy. Physics --
regime (P3), plate count (P1), degree-1/2 collapse (P2) -- decides planetary character at every radius.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT ABOUT WHAT ANY OF THIS SHOWS. Relief in this engine is SHADED, NOT DISPLACED: the height field
only bends the surface normal (perturbAnalytic / perturbFiniteDiff), never geometry, and the instrument layer
refuses to report km for exactly this reason ("Multiplying the sampled field by radius*6371 therefore produces a
confident, wrong number ... ~200x too large"). There is also an undocumented hard saturation downstream of the
whole law -- planet-lod-height.glsl.js:1489-1495 clamps when dot(N', N) < 0.5 -- and the analytic and
finite-difference paths apply different effective gains to the same uniform (the finite-diff path has no lodRamp
term). Any amplitude law is being read through all three. Fix the radius-blindness (a) first, then check the
saturation clamp does not eat the super-Earth branch before judging any exponent by eye.

derivation.whatIsUnknowable:
STATED PLAINLY, BECAUSE "SCIENTIFICALLY PREDICTED FOR SUPER-EARTHS" CAN BE MISHEARD AS "OBSERVED":

1. THERE IS NO MEASURED SUPER-EARTH TOPOGRAPHY. Not weak constraint -- none. No rocky exoplanet surface has ever
   been spatially resolved: no image, no altimetry, no shape model, no topographic spectrum. McTier & Kipping
   2018 (MNRAS 475:4978, arXiv:1801.05814) assess whether it could EVER be detected and conclude it needs
   Colossus/OWL-class apertures plus a Mars-sized planet transiting a white dwarf, and is "unproductive" for
   planets around Sun-like or M-dwarf stars. Byrne et al. 2021 offer their flatness prediction as a test for
   "future generations of telescopes." The Solar System contains exactly one body at or above 0.9 g (Earth), so
   the entire super-Earth branch rests on one point plus theory. Every g <= 1 anchor in the codebase is
   CALIBRATION; everything above is DERIVATION. Those are different kinds of knowledge and the code comments must
   not let a future reader conflate them. The convergence is nonetheless the strongest thing here -- four
   mechanisms from three subfields, two from OPPOSITE tectonic regimes, all landing on h ~ 1/g. That is about as
   good as unobserved physics gets. It is still not a measurement.

2. THE SIGN OF d P(mobile-lid) / dR IS UNRESOLVED AFTER 18 YEARS. Valencia et al. 2007 and O'Neill & Lenardic
   2007 published within months, modelled the same physics, and reached opposite conclusions; Korenaga 2010 says
   size barely matters. Lichtenberg & Miguel 2024 survey the whole list and state the models are "not reaching
   convergence." The crux appears to be whether the depth scale d in the convective-stress denominator
   tau ~ eta*v/d should grow with the planet -- a modelling choice, not a measurement. Water and size are also
   partially degenerate in the models (Valencia: halving yield strength by hydration == doubling planetary mass),
   which is part of why size alone cannot be pinned. THE ENGINE MUST CHOOSE. The proposed choice -- water and
   surface temperature deterministic, radius a seeded sign-ambiguous nudge -- is a declared choice, not a derived
   one, and should be commented as such. Note the amplitude law SURVIVES this dispute intact, because its two
   mechanism routes come from opposite sides of it. What does not survive is terrain CHARACTER.

3. TERRAIN STYLE BRANCHED ON TECTONIC MODE IS UNDERDETERMINED. Linear orogenic belts and continents versus
   volcanic edifices and flood plains, at the level of visual style rather than regime taxonomy, is a taste call.
   Label it as one rather than dressing it in a citation.

4. THE FLEXURAL WAVELENGTH EXPONENT'S SIGN ABOVE ~5 M_E. Boussinesq gives p_C = -0.85 (thinner lid at higher Ra);
   compressible models (Miyagoshi et al. series, NOT RETRIEVED this run) report a much thicker lid at 10 M_E,
   which would flip it toward 0 or positive -- the exact opposite visual (broader, not finer, mountain texture).
   This is the single largest remaining uncertainty in the appearance of a super-Earth.

5. WHETHER THE CRUSTAL YIELD STRENGTH Y ITSELF DEPENDS ON g. Guimond+2022 flag that "surface gravity has a
   nonlinear effect on brittle strength through its influence on porosity and fracture density (Heap et al.
   2017)". If Y rises with g the true amplitude exponent is shallower than 1.0. Nobody retrieved has quantified
   it. It is the one thing that could move the exponent rather than the prefactor, and a real reason not to
   over-commit to 1.588 to three significant figures.

6. ABSOLUTE AMPLITUDES ARE NOT KNOWABLE FROM THE MODELS, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO. Y is uncertain by 5x (100 MPa
   granite -> 7.6 km on Earth; ~500 MPa brittle-ductile max -> 37.8 km). Guimond+2022's stagnant-lid model gives
   RMS dynamic topography of hundreds of metres and ocean-basin capacities < 1 Earth ocean where Venus/Earth/Mars
   observe 3.4/3.3/2.9, and they write: "The peak and RMS elevations of our terrestrial planets are much higher
   than those predicted by the dynamic topography scaling here." TAKE THE EXPONENT, DISCARD THE PREFACTOR,
   NORMALISE TO EARTH. That is why the code's Earth-normalised multiplier is the right shape.

7. WHERE THE g = 1 BREAK SITS, TO BETTER THAN ~1.5x IN g. It is a smooth competition between two curves, not a
   kink. Placing it at g = 1 is chosen because that is where Melosh's ceiling stops over-predicting and because
   it makes the law continuous with Earth = 1 for free. Softening the corner with a min() or a smooth blend is
   scientifically neutral -- the exponents are the constrained part, the corner is not.

8. THE CROSSOVER'S ORIGINAL PROBLEM IS REAL AND ITS SOLUTION IS ENGINEERING, NOT PHYSICS. Making the baked
   plate-Voronoi survive magnification (analytic evaluator or cascaded bake) is a genuine unsolved item in this
   codebase, correctly identified by the existing comment. What is NOT legitimate is resolving it by handing
   planetary character to noise. If the engineering slips, the honest interim is a visibly lower-detail plate
   pattern, never a different planet.

9. A REGIME THE SMOOTH LAWS CANNOT REPRESENT AT ALL. Byrne et al. 2021 "eggshell planets": worlds with a brittle
   lithosphere <~ 5 km -- typically super-Earths that are young, hot, close-in, or radiogenically rich -- support
   "little elevated topography" at any gravity. That is a discrete collapse, not a point on any of these curves,
   and my access to it was second-hand (AGU full text 402). Encode it as a separate kill switch or not at all.

10. TWO DATA POINTS I COULD NOT VERIFY AND KEPT OUT OF THE ARGUMENT: Venus's ~14.6 km dynamic range (USGS product
    page 403; Wikipedia gives no extremes) and Io's ~17.5 km. Neither is load-bearing -- dropping Venus
    STRENGTHENS the key null result (r^2 0.015 -> 0.000). Also unverified this run: Jull & Arkani-Hamed 1995,
    Katayama 2021, Heap et al. 2017, Rogers 2015, Turcotte & Schubert (cited as standard textbook only), Bird
    2003, Pike 1980, Turcotte 1987, Ermakov et al. 2018, Foley et al. 2012, Stamenkovic et al. 2012, and the
    Miyagoshi compressible-convection series.
maxDecisions: FLEXURAL WAVELENGTH SIGN (Family C). Ship p_C = -0.85 (Boussinesq: T_e ~ g^-1/3, lambda_flex ~ g^-1/2), giving ~2x finer mountain/ridge/graben texture on a 1.5 R_E world. The compressible-convection literature (Miyagoshi et al., NOT RETRIEVED this run) reports a much THICKER lid at 10 M_E, which would push p_C toward 0 or positive and produce the opposite visual. Nothing retrieved adjudicates it. DECISION: ship -0.85 as a NAMED constant with the bracket [-0.9, 0.0] and both positions in the comment. This is a priority call (ship the better-supported side now) not a physics finding, and it must not be settled by a UAT screenshot.

SUPER-EARTH REGIME PRIOR. The literature is non-convergent on the sign of dP(mobile)/dR, so the engine must declare weights. DECISION: keep the existing seeded three-way draw (mobile 0.45 / episodic 0.25 / stagnant 0.30) with water and surface-T as the deterministic nudges, widen the seeded band so super-Earths are actually inside it (currently R in [0.87, 1.14] excludes them all), and add radius only as (1 + eps*ln R) with eps seeded on [-0.3, +0.3]. The competing declared choice would be to lean stagnant above 1 R_E on the Solar-System prior (Lichtenberg & Miguel 2024: 'stagnant lid geodynamics may be a better approximation for exoplanets'), which is defensible but rests on a sample of n=1 mobile-lid member and zero members above 1 R_E. Chosen for playable variety over a one-sided prior -- that is a taste call and should be logged as one.

DEGREE-1/2 COLLAPSE ONSET AND BLEND WIDTH. Tackley+2013 and Meier+2021/2024 put the planform collapse toward hemispheric convection 'at high mass' and at 1.34 R_E respectively, but nothing pins a threshold and it is sensitive to the assumed lithospheric yield stress. DECISION: w_deg1(R) = smoothstep(1.5, 2.0, R). Bundled with it, and scientifically neutral either way: whether the g=1 amplitude break renders as a hard kink or a smoothed min() over the two branches -- the exponents are constrained, the corner is not, so pick whichever reads better in-game.

overclaims: THE BREAK AT g=1 IS DECLARED, NOT DERIVED. The section is headed 'WHY THE BREAK AT g = 1 IS PHYSICAL, NOT COSMETIC' but the derivation's own primary source contradicts the location: Guimond 2022 says eq.(21) with Y~100 MPa 'will roughly reproduce the maximum elevations of Venus, Earth, and Mars' — Mars sits at 0.378 g. So the strength ceiling is roughly attained down to ~0.38 g, not slack below 1 g. This belongs in maxDecisions as a fourth declared choice, not in the derived section.

'FOUR INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS ... from three subfields, two of them from OPPOSITE tectonic regimes' — it is at most two. Routes (1) crustal strength, (3) Kite's crustal-thickness contrast, and (4) basalt-eclogite depth are all one lever: a fixed stress or pressure divided by rho*g. Only (2), Guimond's convective dynamic topography, is mechanistically distinct. The convergence claim is the single strongest rhetorical move in the amplitude law and it is inflated roughly 2x.

'STATISTICALLY UNCORRELATED' AND 'PROVABLY WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS' FROM n=5. r^2=0.015 on five points has essentially no power to detect anything; it cannot establish a null. Worse, the quantity being regressed is total dynamic range (max-min), an extreme-value statistic that scales with surface area and sampling coverage — and Mercury's 9.85 km is northern-hemisphere-only while the other four are global. Part of the headline 3.05x Mercury/Mars contrast is therefore definitional, not physical.

SPURIOUS PRECISION. Q_hi=1.588 and a*Q_hi=2.700 are quoted to four significant figures on an admitted bracket of [1.33, 2.20] — a factor of 1.65. The '5% agreement' between the strength route (1.588) and convection route (1.68) is also flattered by the shared +1/a=0.588 term: in the physically meaningful quantity q the two routes differ by 8.8%, and the convection route's own bracket spans q=0.74 to 1.61, a factor of 2.2. Two significant figures is the defensible presentation.

p_C = -0.85 IS PRESENTED WITH OBSERVATIONAL SUPPORT THAT ACTUALLY CONTRADICTS IT (see physicsErrors). Calling Landais+2018 'an OBSERVED cross-check, and it is a strong one' for family C inverts what the data say.

D2 'AUDIT: CONFIRMED CORRECT' AND 'measured over 6x in g' OVERSTATES SILBER+2017. The retrieved abstract's headline is the opposite: the simple-to-complex transition is 'highly sensitive to the choice of the time decay and viscosity constants in the Block-Model of acoustic fluidization' and 'occurs at a larger crater size, if higher impact velocities are considered'. The paper models the 10-26 km range but I did not retrieve a 19-20 km lunar transition value from it. K_DT=3.1 may well be fine; the confidence label is not earned from this source.

P4's 'GENERIC fBm ... IS WRONG IN BOTH REGIMES, AT EVERY RADIUS' IS A RENDERING JUDGEMENT DRESSED AS A PHYSICS FINDING. No retrieved source addresses fBm as a topography generator. The regime taxonomy (Lichtenberg & Miguel Fig. 11) is real and verified; the inference that fBm cannot represent it is the author's, and is aesthetic/structural rather than derived. Label it as such — it is probably right, but it is not a citation-backed result.

'Q_RELIEF = 0.58 IS A RADIUS PROXY IN GRAVITY'S CLOTHING ... IT HAS NO PREDICTIVE CONTENT IN g' IS CONTRADICTED BY THE NUMBERS OFFERED TO PROVE IT (see physicsErrors #1). The conclusion may still be defensible on collinearity grounds, but not on the stated evidence.

P1's CLAIM THAT A FIXED-N SPHERICAL VORONOI 'IS THE PHYSICALLY CORRECT CONSTRUCTION' RESTS ON n=1 PLANET. Both Sornette & Pisarenko and Wilkinson et al. analyse Earth's plates only. The verdict that plates.js is 'CORRECT AS SHIPPED' is probably right but is a one-source result, not a triangulated one.

The data cannot locate a break in g at all. whatIsUnknowable #7 says the break is soft to ~1.5x in g, but 1.5x below g=1 is 0.67, and the source's evidence reaches 0.38. Widen the stated uncertainty to at least a factor of ~2.6 in g, move the break from the derived section to maxDecisions, and note that the choice of g=1 is made because it makes the law continuous with the Earth normalisation for free — which is a legitimate engineering reason, not a physical one.

physicsErrors.error: ROUTE (4) (basalt-eclogite => relief ~ 1/g) IS THE DERIVATION'S OWN INFERENCE, PRESENTED AS CITATION-BACKED, AND THE CITED SOURCE PARTLY CONTRADICTS IT. Guimond 2022 §4 (verified verbatim) gives the isostatic relation h_A = (t_R - t_avg)(rho_m - rho_c)/rho_c — in which g DOES NOT APPEAR — and states the eclogite limit caps peak isostatic h_A 'to about 15 km for a Venus-like case (Jull & Arkani-Hamed 1995)', immediately adding 'However, the depth of this phase transition depends sensitively on the crust thermal structure'.
physicsErrors.correction: The 1/g result requires the extra assumption that transition DEPTH ~ 1/(rho*g) at fixed pressure, which the source explicitly qualifies as thermally rather than purely pressure-controlled. Route (4) is not independent of route (1) (same fixed-pressure/rho-g lever) and is not stated by the source. Drop it from the independence count and relabel it as an inference.

physicsErrors.error: THE GUIMOND COLD/HOT BRACKET M^-0.34..M^-0.74 IS INFERRED FROM A FIGURE CAPTION, NOT STATED BY THE PAPER, AND IS PRESENTED AS 'Their cold/hot bracket'. The paper's Fig. 7 caption gives water-capacity MASS-FRACTION exponents: strength-limited M^-0.9, coolest mantles M^-0.8, hottest M^-1.2. The only mass exponent the paper states for topography is the central h_peak ∝ h_rms ∝ M^-0.5.
physicsErrors.correction: The conversion is CORRECT — I reproduced it. With f = M_cap/M ∝ R^2*h/M and R ∝ M^(1/3.7): f ∝ M^(0.5405 - q_M - 1). Then -0.8 => q_M = 0.341 and -1.2 => q_M = 0.740, exactly the derivation's bracket; and the strength line checks out independently (h~1/g => q_M=0.4595 => f exponent -0.919 vs the caption's -0.9). So the bracket is defensible arithmetic and Q_hi in [1.33, 2.20] stands. But it must be labelled 'derived from Guimond+2022 Fig. 7 capacity-fraction exponents', not quoted as the paper's topography bracket — a reviewer checking the paper for 'M^-0.34' will not find it and will call it fabricated.

physicsErrors.error: FAMILY C's SHIPPED EXPONENT IS CONTRADICTED BY BOTH OBSERVATIONS CITED TO SUPPORT IT — and the derivation applies its own falsification standard asymmetrically. Landais+2018 (verified) finds the SAME ~10 km scale break on Earth, Mars, Mercury AND the Moon, a 6x span in gravity. Crooks et al. (verified) find Earth 10 km vs Venus 50 km, at g = 1.00 vs 0.904.
physicsErrors.correction: Under lambda ~ g^-1/2 (p_C=-0.85 in R), the Moon's break should be 0.1654^-0.5 = 2.46x Earth's and Mars's 1.63x; observed, they are equal — that is evidence for p_C ~ 0, not -0.85. And Venus at 0.904 g should differ from Earth by 1.05x; observed 5x. The 'same gravity, different outcome' argument used to demolish Q_RELIEF (Mercury vs Mars) applies with equal force here (Earth vs Venus) and is not applied. Either ship p_C = 0 as the observationally-supported end of the bracket [-0.9, 0.0], or ship -0.85 while stating plainly that the two observational cross-checks favour the other end. Do not cite Landais as supporting -0.85.

physicsErrors.error: MEIER 2024's DEGREE-1 CONVECTION IS DRIVEN BY TIDAL LOCKING AND LID STRENGTH, NOT BY RADIUS. The retrieved abstract for arXiv:2408.10851 (GJ 486b) attributes hemispheric degree-1 tectonics to day-night surface temperature contrast under tidal locking, and studies 'how the strength of the lithosphere affects the convection pattern'. Radius is a fixed property of that one planet (1.34 R_E), not the varied parameter.
physicsErrors.correction: w_deg1(R) = smoothstep(1.5, 2.0, R) keys the degree-1 collapse purely on radius, which the cited source does not support. Lichtenberg & Miguel Fig. 11 (verified) makes the same split explicitly: A1-3 are rotating regimes, B1-3 are tidally-locked regimes, and hemispheric circulation sits in the tidally-locked branch. Either key w_deg1 on tidal locking / surface-temperature contrast / lid strength (which the engine plausibly already has), or keep the radius trigger and label it DECLARED with Tackley+2013 as the only radius-based support — and first verify Tackley's 'merge into broad downwellings' clause, which I could not retrieve.

physicsErrors.error: WILKINSON+2018 IS CITED AS CORROBORATING SORNETTE & PISARENKO WHEN IT PROPOSES A COMPETING DISTRIBUTION. The derivation says Wilkinson, McElroy & Dummond 2018 'reach the same dimensionless-on-the-sphere result by a different route'. The paper ('Broken Sheets—On the Numbers and Areas of Tectonic Plates', GSA Today 28(6), doi:10.1130/GSATG358A.1 — citation itself fully verified) argues that plate DIAMETERS ARE EXPONENTIALLY DISTRIBUTED, and argues against reading slope changes on log-area/log-frequency plots as evidence for discrete plate populations.
physicsErrors.correction: Exponential-in-diameter is not the same claim as Sornette & Pisarenko's power law in area (0.25+/-0.05). Wilkinson et al. further compare plate mosaics to sediment regions, geologic maps and geopolitical subdivisions, i.e. they read the distribution as generic area-partitioning carrying little geodynamic signal. This is a competing description, not independent corroboration — and it specifically undercuts proposedChange item 7's 'add the fractal small-plate tail', which needs the power-law reading. Recast P1 as: one modelled cross-planet result (Valencia+2007) plus two mutually inconsistent Earth-only statistical descriptions.

physicsErrors.error: 'DIMENSIONLESS ON THE SPHERE => LINEAR SIZE ~ R EXACTLY' IS A NON-SEQUITUR. Both Sornette & Pisarenko and Wilkinson et al. analyse Earth's plates and only Earth's.
physicsErrors.correction: Expressing Earth's plate areas in steradians is a unit choice; it demonstrates nothing about how plate angular size varies with PLANETARY RADIUS, because there is no second planet in either dataset. Delete 'Independent empirical support' from P1. The load is carried entirely by Valencia+2007's modelled L/R = 0.29 -> 0.30 over 1-10 M_E. P1's conclusion (no radius term in plates.js) is probably still right, but it is a single-source modelled result, and the confidence ordering should say so.

physicsErrors.error: WRONG COLUMN OF VALENCIA+2007 TABLE 1. The P3 'increasing with R' chain quotes delta ~ M^-0.45, u ~ M^1.19, sigma ~ M^1.00. Table 1 (retrieved verbatim) gives two columns — isoviscous, then temperature-dependent viscosity: 'Isoviscous plate thickness (delta) 43 km -0.45 -0.29 ... plate's velocity (u) 3 cm/y 1.19 0.87 ... normal stress (sigma) 10 MPa 1.00 1.16 ... plate length (L) 1800 km 0.28 0.29'. The quoted values are all from the ISOVISCOUS column.
physicsErrors.correction: The paper treats the T-dependent case as the physical one ('the more realistic T-dependent-viscosity case'). Those values are delta ~ M^-0.29, u ~ M^0.87, sigma ~ M^1.16. This does not flip P3's direction (sigma still rises), but the attribution should be corrected, and note that L's exponent is 0.28 vs 0.29 across the two cases — P1 used 0.28, the isoviscous one.

physicsErrors.error: THERMAL BOUNDARY-LAYER THICKNESS IS NOT ELASTIC THICKNESS. Family C derives T_e from marginal stability, T_e = [Ra_c*kappa*eta/(rho*alpha*dT*g)]^(1/3) ~ g^-1/3, then substitutes it into the flexural rigidity as an elastic plate thickness.
physicsErrors.correction: The algebra is correct and I reproduced both numbers (flexural parameter alpha = [E*T_e^3/(3(1-nu^2)*drho*g)]^(1/4) = 80.8 km, lambda = 2*pi*alpha = 508 km, matching the stated 81 km and 507 km), and delta ~ g^-1/3 follows correctly from Ra_local = Ra_c. But T_e on real bodies is a mechanical proxy set by thermal age and yield envelope and is typically a fraction of the convective boundary layer — the two are different quantities. Since p_C is already the weakest exponent in the table and is contradicted by the two observational cross-checks, this substitution should be named as an additional assumption rather than left implicit.

physicsErrors.error: AEOLIAN 'GRAVITY DOES NOT APPEAR AT ALL' IS TRUE OF THE FORMULA BUT NOT OF THE PHYSICS. lambda = 53*L_drag with L_drag = (rho_s/rho_f)*d contains no g explicitly.
